items.resolution: Fixed: applyStatus ignores KO'd targets.
items.title: Statuses land on units killed by the same hit
items.detail: applyDamage KOs the unit and wipes its statuses, then the move's effect is applied afterwards. applyStatus has no KO check, so the dead unit keeps Stun / Blind / Para / Silence, and a revive brings it back with that status.
items.evidence: Tambours de Kamowakeikazuchi, Scream of the Banshee, Chain Thunder, Solar Flare, Odin's Wrath. Seen in 9 of 14 logged fights.

items.resolution: Implemented: Water Dragon and Abyssal Current soak their targets for 2 turns; standing in the map's water also makes a unit wet. Wet units walk at 0.8 speed and take x1.5 lightning; ice freezes them for sure or gives a 1d2 chance; fire dries them and lightning or ice spends the soaking; Ice Coffin hits a wet target for 2d10 more; Fire Tornado removes wet from allies; Black Turtle and Kaelgrym are immune. Left: Runik Sea Bound's advantage on a wet field (see its own item).
items.title: Wet status
items.detail: There is no wet status. Water Dragon (Eragon) and Abyssal Current (Black Turtle) carry the wet tag but only deal damage. Nothing reads it: Ice Coffin's +2d10 against a wet target, Fire Tornado removing wet, Runik Sea Bound's advantage on a wet field, and the wet immunity of Black Turtle. The combat AI spec lists the wet combos as supported; they are not.

items.resolution: Implemented: the relic starts asleep and absorbs fire. The first strike with the Awake form wakes it for the rest of the fight: no more absorption, the Sleeping form can no longer be used, and a badge shows that Ifrit is awake.
items.title: Ifrit's Bane Sleeping / Awake
items.detail: Kaelgrym has both relic attacks but no state tells which form he wields, so the fire absorption of the Sleeping form is always on, even when he uses the Awake form. Awake should presumably end the absorption.

items.title: Runik Sea Bound: advantage on a wet field
items.detail: Runik Sea Bound should roll with advantage when the field is wet, and its stun and root should each be a 1d2 chance. The spell has no attack roll in the engine (it deals no damage), so there is nothing to give advantage to, and both statuses always land.
items.resolution: Done. Runik Sea Bound now carries its real effect, 1d2 stun and 1d2 root, each a one in two chance. Against a wet target (soaked, or standing in the map's water) each chance rolls with advantage, the better of two rolls: 75%. A bonus hit still makes both certain. The AI test for the control-then-ally line now asks for 6 of 10 instead of 8, since the stun is no longer sure.

Implemented as specified for single-target blows (basic attacks, single-target moves, bounces, the primary target of a splash). Nat 1 vs nat 1: the blow is rolled and both take half. Nat 1 vs anything else, or a nat 20 defense against an ordinary roll: the attack fails and the defender earns a free action. Nat 20 vs nat 20: a plain hit. Nat 20 vs nat 1: dice x4, and a nat 20 vs an ordinary roll or an ordinary roll vs a nat 1: dice x2; the flat part is not multiplied and 1d2 riders are certain on these hits. A sure-hit still lands on a nat 20 defense. The free action is dash in and strike, do nothing, or cast a spell at the attacker (a single-target spell is one attack roll against them; an area spell is centred on them with the caster rolling the attack and everyone in the blast rolling defense). A person is asked; the bot and headless fights strike when the dash reaches, else pass. A stunned or frozen unit gets nothing.
items.title: Crits (nat 20 / nat 1) are frustrating: a nat 20 does nothing when the foe is out of range
items.detail: Redesign the attack outcome around the attacker's AND the defender's d20. Attacker A hits defender C. (1) nat 1 vs nat 1: damage is rolled and both take half of it. (2) nat 1 vs nat 20: A's attack fails and C gets a free turn to use as they want. (3) nat 20 vs nat 20: a plain hit, no bonus damage. (4) nat 20 vs nat 1: a hit with bonus: 1d2 effects are guaranteed and every damage die is quadrupled (1d6 becomes 4d6). (5) nat 1 vs an ordinary roll: A misses and C may dash to A and make a normal attack, do nothing, or cast a spell. (6) ordinary roll vs nat 1: a hit with bonus: 1d2 effects guaranteed and damage dice doubled (1d6 becomes 2d6). (7) nat 20 vs an ordinary roll: same bonus as (6). (8) ordinary roll vs nat 20: A misses and C gets the same free action as (5). If C answers with a spell, C must make an attack roll, always against A; if the spell is an area, C rolls the attack and A's allies caught in it roll the defence.
items.evidence: Today resolveAttack (combat-logic.js:1896) lets a nat 20 hit and a nat 1 miss whatever the defender rolled, and a crit only pays off when the target is in reach. Open points to settle before building: how the free action fits the turn order, whether it consumes C's own turn, and whether the 'ordinary roll' cases need a threshold.

items.resolution: Implemented: area, cone and splash-bystander moves use the same d20 matrix per victim. The caster's one roll against each victim's own: nat 20 doubles the dice (x4 against a victim's nat 1, plain against a nat 20), an ordinary roll against a victim's nat 1 doubles them, 1d2 riders become certain on those hits; a caster nat 1 turns the blow away from every victim (each earns a free action) unless the victim fumbles too (the victim takes half and the caster takes the same half, once per such victim); a victim's nat 20 against an ordinary roll takes nothing and earns a free action. Ordinary rolls keep the old full / half / none rule, and a sure-hit still lands. Splash bystanders defend against the primary roll the same way.
items.title: Crits do not reach area moves
items.detail: The new nat 20 / nat 1 matrix only governs single-target blows. Area, cone and splash-bystander moves still use the old rule: the caster's nat 20 is a full-damage hit, defenders roll against it, and a caster's nat 1 does nothing special. No bonus dice, no free action for a nat 20 defender, no mutual fumble.

items.resolution: Fixed: a free-action spell is now an ordinary pending action, so its target is offered its reacts before it resolves (for an area spell, each unit in the blast). A pre-armed shield blocks it. It is marked free: it never earns anyone another free action, and when it finishes it concludes the action it answered, so the turn moves on exactly once.
items.title: Free-action spells give the target no react
items.detail: A spell cast as a free action resolves at once: the attacked unit is not offered a react (Phoenix Shroud, shields, reflects), and a pre-armed shield does not stop it. It also never chains into another free action.

items.title: The bot never casts a spell on a free action
items.detail: The bot (and headless fights) strike when the dash reaches and otherwise pass; they never choose a spell, and do not weigh striking against a spell or against doing nothing.
items.resolution: Done. The AI (js/ai/) plans casts, domains and transformations as well as strikes; the old note described the first greedy bot. What it still gets wrong is listed in the per-mechanic items.

Implemented as a data field (inflicts) on each move, with three kinds of hindrance. Earthquake, Quake Wave, Wind Tornado, Vicious Mockery and Azure Dragon Roar leave each target they reach rolling every d20 with disadvantage for one of its turns (hindered). Ice Coffin (Eragon) makes the next defense roll of each target a disadvantage, and only that one (hindered_def, up to 2 turns if never rolled). Field of Corruption gives each target a 1d2 chance of disadvantage on attack rolls for 2 turns (hindered_atk); a bonus hit makes the chance certain. A warded target is spared, a target that evades the area is not touched, a fresh hit refreshes instead of stacking, and Fire Tornado lifts all three from allies.
items.title: Disadvantage riders (disv tag)
items.who: Eragon, Meï, Vorrakan Duskbane, Morrow, Cole Climber, Jay
items.detail: Moves tagged disv should leave their targets rolling with disadvantage: Ice Coffin (next saving throw), Field of Corruption (1d2 turns on attacks), Earthquake, Wind Tornado, Quake Wave, and Azure Dragon Roar ("disadvantage on foe rolls for 1 turn"). They only deal their damage. Smoke Screen and Gravity Up are the only moves that apply disadvantage today.
items.evidence: Casting Azure Dragon Roar and Ice Coffin leaves no disadvantage status on any target. Found by the 2026-10-29 audit: every move was cast in the headless engine and the passives were checked against what combat-logic.js reads.

items.resolution: Implemented: Field of Corruption is now a lingering field (S.fields) centred on the chosen cell, radius 4, lasting 5 rounds counting the one it is cast in. It deals no damage and has no attack roll. Every foe inside meets it at the cast and then once at the start of each of its turns (never twice in a round, and not when it has walked out): para, poison, burn and bleed each on their own 1d2, and a 1d2 chance of disadvantage on attacks. Allies and foes outside are untouched. It is drawn on the map and fades with a log line.
items.title: Field of Corruption: its para, poison and burn are certain
items.detail: The description says 1d2 para + 1d2 poison + 1d2 burn + 1d2 disv atk, but the move has no effect string, so its three statuses come from the tags and every target in the area gets all three every time (20 of 20 casts in the check). Only the disadvantage rider honours the 1d2 now. Give the move an effect of "1d2 para, 1d2 toxic, 1d2 burn".

items.title: Damage-over-time rework (resolved)
items.resolution: Implemented in the engine, the status table and the data renames (Roses, Kaelgrym, Swamp Tribe, Field of Corruption).
items.detail: Done: Toxic is now Poison and Toxic shock is Toxic; Calcinated (2d4 fire) is added. Burn, Poison and Bleed last 3 turns, Calcinated, Toxic and Hemoragie 5. Burn, Poison, Calcinated and Toxic hurt at the start of each turn; Bleed costs its dice once per move, Hemoragie per cell walked. Every application is its own copy with its own timer. Wet puts out Burn (not Calcinated). Mecha are immune to Bleed and Hemoragie; an immunity to the basic form covers the upgrade.

items.title: No move applies Calcinated yet
items.detail: Calcinated exists as a status but nothing in characters.json inflicts it; the old Burn-upgrade moves still apply plain Burn. Decide which moves should upgrade.
items.resolution: Done. Decided move by move: Kaelgrym's Final Brasero always calcinates, Escanor's Cruel Sun does it 1 time in 2 ("1d2 calcinated"). No other move upgrades its Burn. See tests/kaelgrym.test.mjs and tests/dots.test.mjs.

Fixed: getReacts returns nothing for a unit under gel, stun, cocoon or fear, so it gets no react prompt. A unit that is only paralysed (and not stunned this turn) still reacts. Root still only blocks movement.
items.title: A paralysed unit can still react
items.detail: Gel, stun and fear (and a turn lost to a para stun) make a unit skip its turn, but getReacts still offers it reactions while the status lasts. Root only blocks movement. Decide whether control effects should also forbid reacts.

items.resolution: Implemented: the evaluation counts the HP a unit still has to lose to burn, poison and bleed (a weight, dot, the tuner can move). A bleed or haemorrhage already costs HP when a plan walks, as the search plays it on the real engine.
items.title: The bot does not value damage over time
items.detail: evaluate.js does not count the damage a Burn, Poison, Bleed or Hemoragie will deal, so it neither prefers nor avoids stacking them, and it walks freely while bleeding.

items.title: Meï keeps both fields up (resolved)
items.resolution: Field of Flower is now a five-round field of allies: those inside are cleansed and heal 10 HP at the cast and at the start of each of their turns (once per round). Fields have a side (foes or allies) and coexist freely; recasting the same field moves it instead of stacking. The map draws them in two colours and a strip above the action panel lists each with its rounds left.
items.detail: Field of Flower was an instant area heal and regen; only Field of Corruption lingered. Assumed: Flower lasts 5 rounds like Corruption, and its old regen status is replaced by the field.

items.title: Para lasts 3 turns with a 1d2 stun chance each turn (resolved)
items.resolution: Para no longer skips turns by itself. It lasts three of its owner's turns, and at the start of each one a 1d2 roll (a 2) stuns the unit for that turn only. A stun immunity resists the roll. Re-applying refreshes the duration, it does not add a copy.
items.detail: Para used to be a plain one-turn skip, the same as gel.

items.resolution: Implemented: area, cone and field casts carry their aimed cell, so a field rises where the plan puts it; the evaluation values every unit a field works on per round left (a weight, field); a unit in a field against it is offered a move out, a hurt one a move into a field of its side.
items.title: The bot does not understand lingering fields
items.detail: The bot casts Field of Corruption as if it were an area spell aimed at a foe, and Field of Flower as a one-shot heal: it does not value the four turns of exposure, and no unit ever walks out of a field it stands in or avoids walking into one.

items.resolution: Implemented: a passive tagged adv rolls advantage on its attack, defense or spell rolls (Jhin only with sword moves). White also has no range limit and ignores walls within 10 cells; Wind Step no longer promises dodging through walls. Death Presence: every foe of a living Hela makes its first attack of the fight at disadvantage.
items.title: Passive advantage is never rolled
items.who: White, Hela, Sylvanas Nightmare, Jeagen, Jhin, Eragon, Kadgar
items.detail: Advantage written on a passive does nothing: White (Sword of Space: always advantage, attacks from anywhere), Hela (True Weapon Goddess: advantage on all attacks), Sylvanas Nightmare (Banshee: advantage on defense), Jeagen (Wind Step: advantage on defense, dodges through walls), Jhin (Sword Master: advantage on sword rolls), Eragon (Know Advantage) and Kadgar (Knowledge): advantage on spell rolls. The engine reads advantage only from domains, a move's own adv tag and one-shot statuses.
items.evidence: Hela attacked 20 times in a test and no advantage roll was logged. Found by the 2026-10-29 audit: every move was cast in the headless engine and the passives were checked against what combat-logic.js reads.

items.resolution: Implemented: Archmage (+3), Great Staff (+2) and Runik Mage (+1d12) add to the damage of Kadgar's single-target, area and cone spells (dice multiplied on a bonus hit, flat part not). items.detail: The divineSync block is never read. With another Divine Beast present each should gain: Jeagen +1d12 attack and +3 speed for allies; Jay +1d8 attack and 1d6 regen for allies; Zhuqiao +1d10 attack and 1d8 healing plus one debuff removed per ally each turn; Black Turtle -1d8 damage taken for allies and +2 defense.

items.resolution: Implemented for attack rolls: Close Quarters Expert (Zed) applies to blows struck from an adjacent cell (not ranged moves) and Sunken Colossus (Black Turtle) applies while it stands in a water cell. Professional Diver (Kay Climber, Glysain) is still dead: it adds to a constitution roll the simulator never makes.
items.title: Passives gated on a context tag never apply
items.detail: Close Quarters Expert (Zed, +1d4+2 on melee attacks) and Sunken Colossus (Black Turtle, +1d10 in water) use contextHasTag. passiveConditionMet returns false for any condition it does not know, so they never apply. Kay Climber and Glysain's Professional Diver use the same condition on a roll the simulator never makes.

items.resolution: Implemented: one stack per ally that falls, kept for the whole fight, capped at 10; the bonus dice are rolled once per stack.
items.title: Relentless Warrior stacks
items.detail: The passive has maxStacks 10 and the allyKO condition, so it presumably grows with each fallen ally. The engine gives the bonus once whenever any ally is down and ignores maxStacks.

items.resolution: Implemented for dash moves: Fire Rush and Shadow Dash end with one free basic attack on the target. Astrid's reaction version of Shadow Dash is still not implemented.
items.title: Opportunity attacks
items.detail: Fire Rush and Shadow Dash dash to the target but never trigger the opportunity attack their description promises. The engine has no opportunity attacks.

items.resolution: Implemented: Bone Shatter pushes each enemy it hits back 2 cells (stopped by walls, units and domain walls) and Bone Armor is gone for 2 turns. Black Turtle cannot be knocked back, pulled or grounded. Only the area branch knocks back.
items.title: Knockback and immovable
items.detail: Bone Shatter should knock enemies back and strip Oslo's Bone Armor until it regrows; only the damage happens. Black Turtle's Northern Bastion (cannot be moved, knocked back or grounded) does nothing, and pull moves still drag it.

items.resolution: Implemented: guardbreak ignores block reactions and pre-armed shields; dodge, dash and teleport reactions still work. Tiger's Leap range is now 6.
items.title: Guardbreak
items.detail: Tiger's Leap is described as guardbreak. It dashes and hits but can still be blocked; only moves tagged unblockabled ignore blocks.

items.resolution: Fixed: against an area or cone move a dodge react (Hat Form, Lightning Flicker, Zed's Shadow Dash, Bunshin) halves the damage its owner takes; against one target it still dodges completely. These reactions are now reaction-only: they no longer appear as moves to cast on your own turn, where they did nothing.
items.title: Dodge reacts do not halve area damage
items.detail: Bunshin, Hat Form, Lightning Flicker and Shadow Dash are written as "instant dodge against one target, half damage against an area". Against an area move Hat Form and Lightning Flicker change nothing (19 damage with and without the react in a test), and Bunshin shields the whole hit instead of halving it. Cast on its owner's own turn, none of them does anything.
items.evidence: Eragon's Fire Tornado against each reactor, same seed, with and without the react. Found by the 2026-10-29 audit: every move was cast in the headless engine and the passives were checked against what combat-logic.js reads.

items.resolution: Fixed: Stone Skin and Wind's Whim are timed buffs (a new grants field on the move). Stone Skin puts 10 flat reduction on its user for 3 of their turns, Wind's Whim +4 on defense rolls against ranged attacks (anything from more than an adjacent cell, or tagged ranged) for 2 turns; a fresh cast refreshes the old one. Cast on the owner's own turn they work and end the turn; used as a react they no longer stop the blow: they are in place before it lands, and Wind's Whim re-judges an ordinary hit already rolled against the raised total.
items.title: Timed react buffs behave as a single block
items.detail: Stone Skin should take 10 flat damage off every hit for 3 turns; Wind's Whim should give +4 on defense rolls against ranged attacks for 2 turns. Both fall into the generic react branch: they block one attack and last no turns. Cast on the owner's own turn they do nothing, and attacks are not tagged ranged.

items.resolution: Implemented: casting it rolls a d6 and ends the turn. 1: 10 damage to Napoleon (ignores reduction). 2-5: +2d8 on the next attack (basic, single-target or area), spent by it. 6: the next attack counts as a sure natural 20 (always hits, dice doubled under the crit rules, or x4 against a natural 1 defense, plain against a natural 20). The bonus or the fate lasts through Napoleon's next turn.
items.title: Destiny Gamble
items.detail: Roll a d6: 1 deals 10 damage to himself, 2-5 gives +2d8 on the next attack, 6 is a sure hit and a crit (x2). Casting it only logs "uses Destiny Gamble".
items.evidence: Found by the 2026-10-29 audit: every move was cast in the headless engine and the passives were checked against what combat-logic.js reads.

items.resolution: Implemented for basic attacks: when Napoleon's first blow lands he swings a second time at the same target (no second react, never a third). A miss, a fumble or a mutual fumble gives no second blow. Moves and spells are not doubled.
items.title: Dual Wielder
items.detail: Attacks twice when the first attack lands. Napoléon gets one attack per action.

items.resolution: Implemented for d20 rolls: a 1 on Napoleon's attack or defense roll is rolled again, once per turn (it comes back at the start of his turn). The d6 of Destiny Gamble and damage dice are not rerolled.
items.title: Djinn's Luck
items.detail: Rerolls a 1 once per turn (not Destiny Gamble). No reroll exists.

items.resolution: Implemented: a blow carries the higher of its wielder's Authority and its relic's (Mace of Vulkan 5, Tambours 7, Chains of Apophis 8, Balmung 8), less any domain debuff. Hela's Anti-Magic now works: spells deal her nothing and statuses do not land, unless the blow carries Authority 8 or more. Mixed hits (physical + magic) lose only the magic share.
items.title: Authority only pierces Perfect Reflection
items.detail: "Authority 5/7/8" on Mace of Vulkan Strike, Tambours de Kamowakeikazuchi, Chains of Apophis and Balmung is ignored, and Hela's Anti-Magic (immune to magic and status below Authority 8) is a flat immunity that no authority ever pierces. Authority is read for Perfect Reflection and one domain effect, nothing else.

items.resolution: Implemented: Death Presence makes each foe's first attack of the fight roll at disadvantage, and Anti-magic Slash switches the passives of everyone it hits off for 1 turn (damage reduction, roll bonuses, regeneration and shields included).
items.title: Death Presence and Anti-magic Slash rider
items.detail: Death Presence (every foe has disadvantage on its first attack each fight) is not applied. Anti-magic Slash does not disable the target's passives for 1 turn.
items.evidence: Anti-magic Slash cast on two foes: damage only, no status. Found by the 2026-10-29 audit: every move was cast in the headless engine and the passives were checked against what combat-logic.js reads.

items.resolution: Implemented: Heracles returns to life with 1 HP each time he is killed, up to 9 times per fight. Alicia's Loki's Blessing is modelled too: once per fight she rolls two d20s when she would fall, and 10 or more on either keeps her up at 1 HP. Nobody else gets a death save.
items.title: Nine Lives
items.detail: Nine times per fight, return to life with 1 HP when killed. The passive uses deathRoll with maxStacks 9, neither of which the engine reads, so Heracles dies like anyone else. Alicia's Loki's Blessing (two death saves) has no counterpart either: the simulator has no death saves.

items.resolution: Implemented: Battle Tactician is a title that unlocks the Give Orders action. It targets an ally, ends the turn, and gives the ally +2 on its attack rolls until its next turn is over. The +2 follows the engine's usual atkRoll convention (added to the damage of a landed blow). The bot can plan it but the greedy policy does not value it yet.
items.title: Battle Tactician
items.detail: +2 to allies' attack rolls when giving orders. Future Zane has no move that gives orders and the passive has no applyOn, so it does nothing. The combat AI spec lists it as supported; it is not.

items.title: Poison and corruption passives
items.who: Spheras Nightmare, Astrid Nightmare, Dream Hunter
items.detail: Poison Breath (Spheras Nightmare: 1d2 poison or 1d12+8 toxic on nearby enemies each turn) and Toxic Daggers (Astrid Nightmare: 1d2 poison or 1d12 extra on each attack) do nothing. Corruption Bolt (Dream Hunter) adds its +1d10 but never builds up corruption on the target.
items.resolution: Done. Poison Breath and Toxic Daggers use ifPoisoned (a 1d2 poison, or the bonus dice on an already poisoned target); the Dream Hunter builds corruption on every landed blow, never drains, and turns the target at 100. See tests/nightmares.test.mjs.

Implemented: Vorpal Slash (Vorrakan) restores 5 spell slots with its lifesteal. Kaelgrym absorbs incoming fire: the hit does nothing and restores 1 slot. The absorption only works while Ifrit's Bane sleeps (see the Sleeping / Awake item).
items.title: Spell slot restoration
items.detail: Vorrakan's Vorpal Slash should restore 5 spell slots after its lifesteal; Kaelgrym's Ifrit's Bane should absorb fire damage to restore spell slots. The lifesteal works, the slots never come back.

items.resolution: Implemented: Benediction of the Moon also wards the ally against new debuffs for 2 of its turns (granted even when nothing was cleansed). Fire Tornado removes wet and disadvantage (disadvantage, Smoke Screen) from the allies within its blast.
items.title: Cleanse riders
items.detail: Bénédiction of the Moon should also grant 2 turns of immunity after removing a debuff. Fire Tornado should remove wet and disadvantage from allies in the area. Neither rider exists.

items.title: GunRang delayed bonus
items.detail: The boomerang should add 1d4 damage on the next turn. The bounce works, the follow-up does not.
items.resolution: Done. GunRang has followUp 1d4: at the start of Rig's next turn it comes back and hits every target it hit. See tests/rig-glysain.test.mjs.

items.title: Force Lightning vs mecha
items.detail: +2d12 against mecha targets. No unit carries a mecha tag and the engine does not look for one.

items.title: Dragon Breath element
items.detail: The cone should be of a chosen element. It is always untyped magic, so element immunities and the fire/ice interactions never apply to it.
items.resolution: Done. Dragon Breath is three spells, one per element (Fire, Ice, Lightning), each with its element tag, for Kadgar and Eragon. The element is picked by picking the spell. See tests/eragon-oslo.test.mjs.

Implemented: the pillars of a map (columns) are walls for movement, sight and blasts. Locked, secret and portcullis doors start shut, each with hit points (portcullis 15, locked 10, secret 20). A shut door blocks movement and blasts; a portcullis still lets sight through. A unit beside a door can open it with its action, or break it with a basic attack, and a damaging area or cone move wears down every door in its blast. Spawn cells now stay in the largest region reachable with every shut door closed, and off the pillars. The AI snapshot carries the door state. New maps: Sunken Hold of the Serpent Knight, Wayrock Maze.
items.title: Pillars and closed doors
items.detail: Pillars were walkable floor, and locked, secret and portcullis doors were open gaps. On Wayrock Maze one team started walled in with only 22 reachable cells.
items.where: dungeon-loader.js · buildWalkableGrid, buildMap; combat-logic.js · hasLos, handleOpenDoor, handleAttackDoor

items.resolution: Implemented: a closed door beside the bot can be opened with its action; when every foe is walled off it walks to the nearest door; area casts carry a centre, so they wear doors down; walking distances are cached per set of open doors. The bot never breaks a door (opening is always at least as good). A secret door is still drawn grey and a locked door has no key.
items.title: The bot ignores closed doors
items.detail: The bot never opens or breaks a door, and its area casts carry no centre, so they do not wear doors down. Single-target spells cannot be aimed at a door either. A secret door is drawn grey on the map instead of looking like wall, and a locked door has no key to find.

items.resolution: Implemented: tools/tune.mjs plays two sets of evaluation weights against each other (SPSA, head-to-head, both seatings) on random matchups and the three maps, with no model and no tokens. See docs/ai-runner.md. First measured run (2026-10-31): 540 iterations found no gain; the best set scored 50.6% (interval 45.7-55.5%) against the start weights over 400 held-out fights, so evaluate.js was left unchanged. An 8-hour run with 300 sims per decision followed.
items.title: The bot's weights had to be tuned by hand
items.detail: Tuning the eight evaluation weights meant running fights and editing numbers by hand in a long session.

items.resolution: Implemented: Chronos, Monarch of Time, in characters.json and main.js (sheet, domain, Guild and Duranmoran entries; 520 HP, Authority 9, Complet domain Chronostasis whose owner regains HP, slots or a Thread at random each turn). He beats Hela in about 70% of 100 greedy-brain duels (tools/sim.mjs). New engine pieces: Rewind (onDeath, once per fight, back to his HP and place of two rounds ago), Decay (necrotic damage over time, one more die each turn), Withering Hour (a hostile move that also arms its caster, each landed basic attack then cuts max HP and the cuts stack), Borrowed Time (extraAction: the action comes back). The search bot cannot plan a second action, so it plays Borrowed Time poorly.
items.title: Chronos, the god of time, is not on the roster
items.detail: A primordial god from before the Aurora, first met as the Guild master. Stasis, Withering Hour, Three Threads, Two-Faced Door, Borrowed Time and Rewind hint, without naming them, at the Norns, Thoth, Kala and Janus he absorbed. Also: a natural 20 that lands can no longer be reacted to (block, dodge or teleport), for every unit; Stasis really stuns for 2 full turns; all his spells cost 1 slot. Not done: a retune of the bot with him in the roster. The 70% figure is measured with the greedy brain, which does not open domains.

items.resolution: Fixed: Embers of Life heals only allies within 8 cells and never Zhuqiao; Undying Flame is 1d10 instead of 2d10; Phoenix Shroud costs 9 ki instead of 6. Every Divine Beast synergy aimed at allies (Western Gale, Dragon Blessing, Phoenix Grace, Northern Depths) now spares its owner; the owner's own bonuses (attack dice, Tidal Anchor) are unchanged. Not measured: no duels were run after the change.
items.title: Zhuqiao heals and cleanses herself far too much
items.detail: Embers of Life healed every living ally on the map, herself included, whatever the distance; Phoenix Grace healed and cleansed her each round; Undying Flame added about 11 HP a turn under half health. With 85 HP, speed 18, flight and a block, she was close to unkillable in a pair of Divine Beasts.
items.where: characters.json · Zhuqiao; combat-logic.js · divineEffects, the hpPerTurn passives and the Divine Beast healing

items.resolution: Implemented: an opponent picker on the combat selection screen (S.aiTeam, kept in localStorage); a driver asks the bot on its turns and reacts through applyPlan and settleReacts; the action panel and react overlay are hidden for bot units. Tested headless.
items.title: No way to play one team against the bot
items.detail: Every fight on the combat page was hot-seat: a person had to play both teams.

items.title: acceptance --quick fails its strength stage
items.detail: The strength stage needs 80% wins against the greedy brain over 8 fights (seeds 1..1, 500 sims). It scored 62.5% before the Chronos merge and 75% after it, so the failure is not new. With 8 fights the stage is mostly noise, and it makes tests/acceptance.test.mjs fail. The Zhuqiao 5v5 matchup (Zhuqiao +4 vs Jaina +4) is one of the two matchups used. Also not measured: the bot with Chronos on the roster, and Zhuqiao after her nerf.

items.title: Summoning
items.who: Irina, Leonidas, the Sorcerer Master, Annastasia, Krux & Acronix
items.detail: The engine now creates units mid-fight (spawnSummon in combat-logic.js): a move with a summon field {unit, count} calls units beside the caster, which join its team and act right after it; a sheet with a companion field (Sorcerer Master: Floating Head) has it from round 1. Done: Flaming Bird (1 ki, one Fire Spirit), Living Bomb (bursts every Fire Spirit on its own spot, radius 3), Golem Creation (1d4 Golems), Floating Head. Rules: a summon never counts toward victory, falls with its caster, and is not a roster pick. Sacrifice Mark (Annastasia): at the start of the battle she marks a random enemy; when it falls she calls one Demon (its max HP under 70) or two (70 and above), and the mark always passes to another enemy (after a death or a Taboo). The Demon sheet (tags summon, monster, oni; 70 HP) has Dragon Slayer, Claws 2d8+2 and Oni Beam (1d12 + 1d8 splash). Taboo: half her current HP and a spell slot spring the mark at once (the victim lives); it needs a living mark, and the AI does not cast it. Summoning Portal (Krux & Acronix) calls a Time Remnant: any roster character (not a summon), named "Time Remnant X", picked in a list under the ability. Cost in spell slots by its max HP: round(1 + 4 x ((HP - 50) / 70)^2), at least 1 (50 HP = 1, 95 = 3, 120 = 5, 180 = 15). At most 2 stand at once; each plays 2 turns then fades, or falls with Krux & Acronix. The AI never casts it. The AI casts a summon while fewer than 3 of that kind stand, and bursts the spirits once a foe is within reach of one. Vorrakan's chains are a separate unique case (see decide-chains-units). Irina's Child of the Phoenix is her burn immunity, done. Flaming Bird is a normal action, not the instant the Google Doc names, so that the greedy policy can cast it.
items.resolution: Done. Every summon of the sheets is modelled: Flaming Bird, Living Bomb, Golem Creation, Floating Head, the Demons of Sacrifice Mark (with Taboo) and the Time Remnants of Summoning Portal. Left aside on purpose: the AI never casts Taboo, Demon Pact or the Summoning Portal.

items.title: Hunter mark: x2 damage, advantage on defense
items.detail: Apex Predator / Huntress: at the start of the battle a random enemy is marked. The marked target takes x2 damage, the owner has advantage on every defense throw against it. Vampire Sienna also restores 100% HP and spell slots when the target dies. Descriptions only.
items.resolution: Done. At the start of the battle each hunter (passive tag huntMark) marks one random living enemy, never a summon. Damage rolled by her attacks and spells against it is doubled (before a mutual-fumble halving); she defends against it with advantage. Apex Predator (huntFeast) restores Vampire Sienna to full HP and spell slots when the mark dies. Not doubled: damage over time and the splash around a main target. See tests/hunter-mark.test.mjs. Easter egg: when Sienna falls she has a 1 in 100 chance to rise whole as Vampire Sienna (sheet field reborn).

items.title: Blood Magic and SteamGun
items.detail: Vampire Sienna: every hit drains 50%, overheal becomes a blood shield, regenerates 10 HP a turn, Bite drains HP, spell slots and ki. Sienna: a normal attack after a technique applies burn; two techniques in a row halve the damage. Descriptions only. Hypnosis (control) is tagged but unchecked.
items.resolution: Done. Vampire Sienna: every hit she lands heals her for 50% of the damage dealt (drainPct; Blood Drain and Bite keep their 100%), all her healing past full HP becomes a blood shield except the 10 HP regeneration she gets each turn, Bite takes 1d4 spell slots and 2d4 ki, and Hypnosis, when it succeeds, lets her choose the target's next action (the puppet tag, as Puppeteer). Sienna: SteamGun reads only Range Mode and Rodent Mode (steamMode): a basic attack right after one burns, one mode right after the other halves the damage; Healing Potion does not count. Battle Medic now adds +3 to healing moves (healRoll), and Basic Training (+1, also Simo) is a weapon roll only. See tests/blood-magic.test.mjs.

items.title: Geminy, Vision of Time, time moves
items.detail: Two actions a turn (Geminy), immunity to natural 1 and to disadvantage, and Pause / Play / Forward (drain 1d4 slots from an area) / Backward (heal all damage since last turn). The engine now has two actions a turn (the divinity tag, see mech-divinity), but it forces the two to differ: decide whether Geminy's do. The rest is descriptions only.

items.title: Holy Duel
items.detail: Targets one adversary: Arthur gains 2x the target max HP, advantage on every roll against it and 4d20 damage against it. Only the 4d20 hit is modelled (once per fight); the HP gain and the advantage are not.
items.resolution: Done. Casting Holy Duel binds Arthur to the target for the rest of the fight: he gains twice its max HP (max and current), and has advantage on every attack, spell and defense roll against it, besides the 4d20 hit (once per fight).

items.title: Stance Switch, Hypnosis, Guard
items.detail: Ouroboros: defense stance +4 to defense rolls / attack stance +2 to attack rolls. Hypnosis stuns with a 1d2 chance of control. Argo: Guard prepares a block for an ally for 1 turn, and Iron Sentinel gives +3 defense when guarding. Lan Na Zha (block, then dash) is tagged react + dash and may not chain both. Descriptions only.

items.title: Static Charge and Thunder Step
items.detail: Static Charge: the next attack gains +2 per step walked. Thunder Step: damage is bounce count x 1d8 (modelled as a plain bounce). Descriptions only.

items.title: High-Pressure Mastery and Fluid Parry
items.detail: All attacks should have armor penetration (only the base attack and Crushing Weight carry arPen). Fluid Parry is an instant counter-attack react; there is no counter react in the engine. Crushing Weight's prone is an effect string only.

items.title: Master Blacksmith and Heat Haze
items.detail: Master Blacksmith reinforces an ally's weapon (+1d4). Heat Haze is an instant aoe react giving allies +4 to defense rolls. Solid Flames adds 1d4 and a 1d2 burn on every attack. Descriptions only, except the +1d4.

items.title: Star Link table
items.detail: Star Link rolls 1d100 to link to a star "see stars table". The table is not in the Google Doc: it is needed. Nothing is rolled yet.

items.title: Gravity Master and Black Hole
items.detail: Flying adversaries must save every turn or lose flight for a turn. Black Hole is a react that absorbs a ranged attack (Vorrakan's Black Hole is a different move). Descriptions only.

items.title: Acid Armor, Lightning Rod, Energise
items.detail: Ivy: melee attackers take 1d4 and a 1d2 toxic chance. Electro: absorbs every electric attack (Storm Body of Jay Azure Dragon is the closest existing behaviour). Energise: an ally rolls with advantage on everything next turn (adv_next exists for one roll, not for all rolls). Descriptions only.

items.title: Gem knights: hit count, petrification, psy save
items.who: Rubis Ignir, Emeraud Brannoc, Amethyst Ysmar, Saphir Thalor, Diamant Dunmara
items.detail: Rubis: counts the hits taken, Retribution Shard deals hitCount x 0.8 then resets. Emeraud: every hit adds a petrification stack; Petrify rolls 1d20 + stacks to petrify. Amethyst: Crystal Resonance makes targets save (psy) or attack their allies. Saphir: Prismatic Guard reflects magic damage. All five: Retribution Shard (1d2 chance of 1d6 to everyone around when hit) and Prismatic Guard -20 flat magic damage. Descriptions only; Diamant's +8 armor and the shared kit work.
items.resolution: Done. Retribution Shard (Emeraud, Amethyst, Saphir, Diamant): when hit and still standing, a one in two chance of 1d6 to every foe within 2 cells (never chains between gem knights). Rubis counts the hits he takes; his Retribution Shard technique deals hits x 0.8 (rounded down), then the count resets, and it is unavailable at zero. Emeraud: each blow that lands leaves a petrification stack on the target; Petrify rolls 1d20 + stacks, 20 or more stuns it 3 turns (stone) and clears the stacks. Amethyst: Crystal Resonance puts every target that fails its defense roll against the blast under her control for its next action (the same puppeteered status as Hypnosis, standing for the psy save). Prismatic Guard: a reaction offered only against a spell, which then loses 20 once (it did nothing before); Saphir keeps the reflect version. Petrify (DC 20, stone = a 3-turn stun) confirmed by the user; shard radius 2 and foes only are still my choice. The AI uses none of the new moves.

items.title: Nexo knights: Dead Eye, Faster, Sturdy, Leader
items.detail: Aron: ranged attacks cannot be dodged. Lance: takes half damage from anything with a lower initiative than his. Axel: 1d4 chance to ignore damage. Clay: the first time an ally would die he takes the damage instead. Descriptions only.

items.title: Destiny's Fire and The End Slash thresholds
items.detail: Destiny's Fire starts at 30 HP (mono 2d20, aoe 1d20+1d12, then +1d10 on all attacks to the end of the battle). The End Slash needs less than 25 HP (mono 4d20, aoe 2d20 + burn + para + 1d8 heal). Both are plain relics with no HP threshold. Motion Channel (unblockable, burn) and Motion Guard (ultimate block) are tags only.

items.title: Demon Pact, Sacrifice Mark, Taboo
items.detail: Demon Pact: -10 HP buys 1 spell slot, and she heals 1d10 when dealing damage. Sacrifice Mark picks a random enemy and summons one or two demons when it dies. Taboo halves her current HP and triggers the mark at once. Descriptions only.
items.resolution: Done. Demon Pact heals her 1d10 whenever she deals damage. Sacrifice Mark: at the start of the battle (and again after each spring) a random enemy carries the mark; its death calls one Demon (max HP under 70) or two, and the mark passes to another enemy. Taboo halves her current HP and a slot to spring the mark at once. Demon Pact's slot purchase is a move of its own, an instant: 10 HP for 1 spell slot, as often as she can pay, never her last HP, and not above her maximum slots. The AI does not use it.

items.title: Aura of Terror, Psychic Link, Theroxian Mastery
items.detail: Done so far: auras are in the engine (a passive with a target and a radius), so Aura of Terror (enemies within 4 cells, -3) and Psychic Link (+2 to her team within 8) work, and allRolls now counts for attack, defense and magic rolls (it also turns on Jack of All Trade, Heavenly Champion and War Banner Carrier, which did nothing before). Left: Theroxian Mastery, Containment Spell, Immobilization Seal. Original text: Aura of Terror: -3 to the attack rolls of enemies around her. Psychic Link: +2 to all friendly rolls (the allRolls passive exists but is untested as an ally aura). Theroxian Mastery: her debuffs cannot be removed. Containment Spell: a 40 HP energy cage that only breaks from outside; Immobilization Seal stops a dash or blink as a react.
items.resolution: Done. Aura of Terror: enemies within 4 cells of Rox get -3 on their attack rolls. Psychic Link: +2 to every attack, defense and magic roll of her team within 8 cells, herself included (the engine now reads auras and allRolls). Theroxian Mastery: the hindrances she lays on a foe are marked sticky and no cleanse lifts them. Containment Spell (1 slot): a 40 HP energy cage; the prisoner is stunned and rooted and cannot be freed by cleansing, every blow from outside lands on the cage, damage over time on its own turn still reaches the prisoner, and the cage goes when it breaks or when Rox falls. Immobilization Seal (1 slot, 2 round cooldown): when a foe within 10 cells dashes or blinks with a spell, a ready Seal stops the move automatically (the move is spent anyway); it is not offered as a normal react. The AI does not cast Containment Spell on purpose.

items.title: Tides of Misfortune, Curse Reflect, Entropy Field
items.detail: Once a turn an enemy must reroll a die that succeeded. Any debuff aimed at him is sent back to its source. Entropy Field: a field where 2 and 3 count as critical fails for enemies. Descriptions only.
items.resolution: Done. Tides of Misfortune: once a round, the first foe die that succeeds against Zarkt's side (a blow that lands, or a defense that holds against his side's blow) is rolled again and the new roll stands; automatic, no prompt. Curse Reflect: any hindrance a foe lays on Zarkt, by a move or by a basic attack rider, is applied to its sender instead. Entropy Field (1 slot): a 4 cell field for 3 rounds in which a 2 or a 3 rolled by a foe counts as a natural 1. The AI does not cast Entropy Field on purpose.

items.title: Hive Mind and Chitin Armor
items.detail: Hive Mind: +x to each roll for each ally, Drix counts as one, poison stacks. Chitin Armor: -20 physical, +10 area damage, +10 fire and lightning damage taken (only the physical part is modelled). Nesting Strike's 10x1d2 poison is reduced to a 1d2 poison effect.
items.resolution: Done. Hive Mind: +1 to Drix attack and defense rolls for each living ally, himself counted. Chitin Armor: -20 physical as before, and now +10 from area blows (aoe damage carries an area tag), +10 fire and +10 lightning, applied before the reduction. Nesting Strike lays ten 1d2 poison chances, which stack, and a 1d2 paralysis. Not done: the poison stack has no cap or special rule beyond stacking.

items.title: Life Siphon and Decay Wave
items.detail: Life Siphon drains 1d6+4 HP on touch. Decay Wave deals an extra 1d10+5 against energy, life and plant targets. Bandage Coil roots the target to him while draining. Siphon is modelled as hpPerHit; the rest is descriptions only.
items.resolution: Done. Life Siphon was already modelled (hpPerHit). Decay Wave now deals its extra 1d10+5 to every living target (anything but mechas and golems, which carry the lifeless tag; the roster has no energy, life or plant tags). Bandage Coil already worked: a necrotic hit that roots the target and heals Kur for the damage dealt.

items.title: War Banner, Blood Tracker, Asia style
items.detail: War Banner: +2 to all ally rolls within 10 m. Blood Tracker: +3 perception, +1d6 vs wounded targets (the wounded condition does not exist). Asia style: bleed 1d4 on hit, convertible to hemorrhage 2d4. Atila has no move yet.

items.title: Ranger, Shadow Master, Cook: utility and stealth rolls
items.detail: Battle Medic (+3 healing roll, heal as a bonus action), Ranger (+3 lockpicking/perception/defuse/set trap), Shadow Master (+2 stealth), Cook (+1) use roll kinds the engine has no applyOn for (healRoll, stealthRoll; utilityRoll is only partly used). Libra's Reequip (change weapons) and Arrow Dancer (+3 defense vs ranged) are descriptions only. Update: Battle Medic is done (Sienna, Simo, Libra): +3 to every healing roll, and a once-a-turn bonus-action heal of 1d6+3 on self or an adjacent ally; see tests/battle-medic.test.mjs. Still open: Ranger (lockpicking, defuse, set trap), Shadow Master (+2 stealth) and Cook, which need stealthRoll and utilityRoll.

items.title: Phoenix Feathers and Grow Spurt
items.detail: Phoenix King: Phoenix Feathers resurrect a target (4 charges) and regenerate all spell slots; modelled as a relic with 4 charges, the slot regeneration was not checked. Phoenix Prince: Grow Spurt turns him into the Adult form for 4 turns (modelled as a once-per-fight technique, not a timed form switch); Phoenix Hug heals both, then again next turn.
items.resolution: Done. Phoenix Feathers (4 charges) revive the target at half HP and now give it back all its spell slots. Grow Spurt is a real form (like Susano's Nirvana): the Prince takes the Adult Form (+20 HP, +3 slots, Flaming Dash, Phoenix Hug, Phoenix Feather) until the end of the fight (balance change: it first lasted 4 turns); once per fight. Phoenix Hug heals the target and the Prince, and both again when the Prince next turn starts.

items.title: Sunshine aura and calcinated stacks
items.detail: Deals 1d4 damage around him and gains +5 attack and +5 defense for each calcinated stack on the target. Cruel Sun applies calcinated through the effect string; the aura and the per-stack bonus are descriptions only.

items.title: Undying Army and Anti-Magic seals
items.who: Sword Master, Sorcerer Master, Anti-magic ghouls, Amalgame
items.detail: Regeneration of 10/20 HP a turn and -10/-20 flat magic damage are modelled. Amalgame's Slime (-10 physical), Thousand Cuts (8d4) and the anti-magic seal (magic sealed for 1 turn) rely on existing tags that were not checked in a fight.

items.title: Blessing of Oberon and Toxic Pollen
items.detail: Self aoe heal of 1d6 each turn (modelled like Embers of Life, radius 4, untested) and a cone with 1d2 para and 1d2 poison (only the para is an effect).

items.title: Storm End
items.detail: A self aoe taunt for 2 turns that also deals 1d12+4 damage. The taunt tag exists (Baal), the combined damage is untested.

items.title: Weapon Creation
items.detail: Creates a weapon. No rule on what it gives; needs a decision.

items.title: Cryostase
items.detail: Removes bleed and burn, then heals 1d8+8. The cleans tag removes statuses but whether it covers damage over time was not checked.

items.title: Mountain's Weight and prone
items.detail: Immovable units are now immune to the root status as well as knockback and pulls (Nokt, Bentei, Maya). Cannot be knocked prone or pushed back (immovable tag). Prone is not an engine status, so Earthquake Slam and Crushing Weight only have a text effect.
items.resolution: Done. Immovable units (Nokt, Bentei, Black Turtle) cannot be pushed back, pulled, rooted or knocked prone. Prone is now a status: Maya's Crushing Weight and Bentei's Earthquake Slam each give a 1d2 chance of it, it lasts through the target's next turn, and for now it simply puts every d20 of its owner at disadvantage (the user's call; standing up and the melee advantage against it are not modelled). A cleanse lifts it, and Opportunist (Argo) now reads stunned or prone. Maya is not immovable, only the owner of the prone move.

items.title: Chi Overdrive and Finest Sword of Chima
items.detail: +/-1d8 damage (modelled as +1d8 on attack rolls), immune to stun, fear and para (not set in immunities), advantage on all weapon-related rolls.

items.title: Range / Rodent / Blade modes
items.detail: The doc writes them as three modes of one weapon. Modelled as Range Mode (mono hit only, the 1d10 aoe part is a description), Rodent Mode (cone) and the Blade Mode base attack.
items.resolution: Done. Range Mode is a long-range mono shot (range 12) with a 1d10 splash around the target; Rodent Mode is a flamethrower cone. Both carry Precise Shot (ranged) and Basic Training, and both feed SteamGun.

Done as a unique case, not a companion: Vorrakan holds two chains of 150 HP (not units). The Chain Guard react sends a blow to them; the two-charge Chains of Apophis relic (Authority 5) grabs a foe and cannot be cleansed. See tests/chains.test.mjs.
items.title: Left and Right Chain as units
items.detail: The Google Doc gives two 150 HP chains with "End of all life" (wrap around the target, drain HP and spell slots; if not broken in time, steal and store the power). They are not on the site (Chains of Apophis is only a relic). To decide: separate sheets, summons, or one move. The summon engine now exists (see mech-summons), so the chains could be units called by a Vorrakan move.

To decide, form by form, which side is right.
items.resolution: Closed. Every form was settled in its own character decision (Susano, Sensei Lloyd, Climbers, Wolf Clan General, Cinder). Last gap: Kay's dragon form gets the doc's 2 dragon spells as +2 spell slots while it lasts (transformation.spellSlot).
Done: Fire Spirit, Golem and Floating Head keep their sheets (tag summon) but are no longer offered on the team selection grid or picked by the tuner; they only exist when called.

items.detail: They were added as normal sheets (tag summon) so they can be picked in a fight. If they should only exist as summons, remove them from the roster once the summon mechanic is in.

items.title: Yangshi has no sheet
items.detail: The Murim tab only says "Yangshi 60hp :" with nothing else. Not added.

items.resolution: Done: the sheet tag divinity (Hela, Chronos, Susano in Nirvana) gives two actions a turn that must differ (basic attack, each ability, transform, domain and door count as one action each; instants cost none). Borrowed Time adds a third. A tag also lets passives target divinities: Jeagen's Divine Hunter deals +1d20 to them (condition targetHasTag). See tests/divinity.test.mjs.
items.title: Divinity: two different actions a turn, and damage against divinities
items.detail: Final Reckoning (Hela, from Resurrection or cast) adds a third action a turn on top of Divinity's two. Borrowed Time used to need an action already spent, which the engine never left open; it now grants its extra action whenever it is cast.
